Maria (PM): quick sync — after last night's routing outage I sketched a small PRD + RFC addendum with focused acceptance criteria and runbook guardrails. posting here for triage and prioritization. TL;DR: require automatic fallback to smaller quantized model at TTFB > 300ms for 3s window, add health-check backoff and explicit routing fallback policy, and add two runbook play items for oncall. link: https://redwood.internal/prd/rfc/fallbacks-postoutage

AJ (EngRuntime): scanning it now. can you paste the core acceptance criteria here? want to check perf tradeoffs + cost delta.

Maria (PM): sure — from doc: 1) When primary variant latency > 300ms P50 for >=3s we route new requests to fallback variant within same capacity tier. 2) Rollback window: auto-recover attempts at 30s intervals, with exponential backoff capped at 5m. 3) Fallback must preserve top-1 safety filters and token-level logging. 4) Metrics: measure end-to-end request latency, fallback-rate, and quality-regression on a holdout prompt set (<1% drop in preferred metric). 5) Owner: eng-runtime for implementation, SRE for runbook changes, Product for rollout gating.

Sam (SRE): ok, runbook items I want: a) explicit detection alert (anomaly if routing-fallback > 2% for 5m), b) play to force-override fallback, c) fallout checklist (cache flush, rewarm KV cache, verify model weights). Also add a single cmd snippet for ops: ```# force revert to primary
redwood route set --model primary-v3 --force --reason "post-incident revert"
# rewarm cache
redwood cache warm --model primary-v3 --samples 1000
```

Jen (Oncall): I ran the commands last night. suggest we add step numbers and expected visible signals in Console (route change visible under /routes, fallback rate chart). Also add a line that says: notify product + infra in #incidents when fallback sustained > 5m.

AJ (EngRuntime): perf note: routing switch itself is cheap but quantized fallback model can increase generation time slightly (token throughput drop ~10% in our bench). we should add acceptance threshold for throughput drop or QPS floor so downstream SLAs don't break. propose: fallback only when latency breach is causing estimated SLA violation, or when fallback can maintain >=70% throughput of primary under same batch sizes.

Maria (PM): good point. update: add acceptance criterion: fallback must not reduce 95th throughput by more than 30% vs primary, otherwise prefer regional routing to secondary capacity. I'll add that to PRD.

Leo (Product): priority question — is this a P0 for next sprint or P1 backlog item? from customer asks it's high for a few enterprise customers. suggestion: break into two phases: Phase A (detection + emergency fallback + runbook) for next sprint (P0), Phase B (throughput budget, routing policy refinements, UI exposures) for following. thoughts?

Priya (Design): for Phase A we should also add small UX copy for fallback states in SDK responses and Console so clients can detect degraded but safe responses. propose a `x-redwood-fallback: true` header and a short note in the event payload.

Sam (SRE): +1 on header. add to runbook step: check request headers for `x-redwood-fallback` and alert if client sees >10% false-positive rates.

Maria (PM): sounds like consensus. I'll update the PRD: split into Phase A/B, add acceptance criteria AJ suggested, include runbook steps from Sam and Jen, and add the SDK header from Priya. action items: - Maria: update PRD and RFC by EOD today - AJ: rough perf estimate + microbench by Tue - Sam/Jen: add runbook play steps and alert rules - Priya: draft header UX and SDK change note

incident-bot: incident summary posted: outage window 2026-03-19T23:12Z–2026-03-19T23:48Z, root cause: routing decisions under heavy tail requests. linked PRD addendum: https://redwood.internal/prd/rfc/fallbacks-postoutage

AJ (EngRuntime): noted. I'll also add a small experiment plan to validate quality regression on holdout set before enabling auto-fallback.

Maria (PM): thanks everyone. if no objections I'll create the PR and tag owners. please react or reply with blockers. :thumbsup:
